newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly lower on Monday on a lack of new domestic A share issues, which reduced demand for funds on the market, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded three-day contract fell to 10.10 percent from 11.00 percent last Friday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose to 5.5 million lots from 4.6 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills. No new A share issues are scheduled for the next few days.
But the strong performance of the A share markets prevented the contracts from falling more sharply, traders said.
The China Securities newspaper said on Monday a central state-debt depository would start operations shortly.
Traders said trading volume on the Shanghai market would fall sharply once the central depository starts operations.

Repo rates are expected to fall slightly over the next few days, traders said. Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed on Monday with sentiment weak due to the poor debut of a new issue which listed today, traders said.
The newly-listed three-year T-note that matures in May 2000 was the most actively traded contract, closing at 97.65 yuan against its face value of 100 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 1.4 million lots from 1.1 million lots.

Traders said the poor performance of the new note depressed similar types of state debt contracts with interest paid on maturity. But the state debt contracts with interest paid on an annual basis were not affected, they said.
Traders said they expected spot contracts to move narrowly around current levels over the next few days.
